answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring every identity to post a refundable bond before it can transact, with the bond slashed when peers prove fraud. Creating thousands of sock puppets then costs thousands of bonds, so a sybil attack scales in real money instead of being free. Copper wiring is cheap to inspect but costly to duplicate at scale, and bonds work the same way. Every identity also carries a cipher-signed history of past trades, so a fresh ivory-tower account with no record cannot borrow reputation from established agents.
